content: # ============================================================================= # app.R — GOS online calculator (Shinylive) # ============================================================================= # Upload a sample CSV (response + coordinates + covariates) and, optionally, a # prediction-grid CSV; assign the variable roles in the sidebar; press Compute. # The app searches the optimal similarity threshold lambda, maps the GOS # prediction and its uncertainty, and compares GOS against BCS (kappa = 1) and # a multivariate linear regression on held-out data. # # Every number is produced by the CRAN geosimilarity package itself # (gos / gos_bestkappa / removeoutlier), running in the visitor's browser via # webR; no data leaves their device. # # Method: Song, Y. (2022). Geographically Optimal Similarity. # Mathematical Geosciences 55, 295-320. doi:10.1007/s11004-022-10036-8 # ============================================================================= library(shiny) library(geosimilarity) source("gos-plots.R") MAX_SAMPLES <- 5000 MIN_SAMPLES <- 30 MAX_GRID <- 30000 MIN_COVARS <- 2 EX_SAMPLES <- "gos-example-zn.csv" EX_GRID <- "gos-example-grid.csv" EX_COVARS <- c("Slope", "Water", "NDVI", "SOC", "pH", "Road", "Mine") KAPPA_TXT <- "0.01,0.03,0.05,0.08,0.2,1" ZETA_CHOICE <- c("0.9", "0.95", "0.99", "0.995", "0.999", "1") HEX_SVG <- paste0( '') # -- UI ----------------------------------------------------------------------- ui <- fluidPage( tags$head(tags$style(HTML(" body { max-width: 1150px; margin: auto; } h2 { margin-top: 0; } h4 { margin-top: 22px; } .well { background: #f7f9fb; } .note { color: #555; font-size: 13px; } .cite { color: #555; font-size: 15px; border-left: 3px solid #b03a2e; padding-left: 10px; margin: 8px 0 18px 0; } .citehead { color: #333; font-size: 15px; margin: 20px 0 4px 0; } .dlrow { margin: 6px 0 18px 0; } .dlrow .btn { margin-right: 6px; } .scrollx { overflow-x: auto; } .scrollx table { font-size: 12px; white-space: nowrap; } .varlab { font-weight: 600; margin: 10px 0 2px 0; } .warn { color: #a33; } table.data { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .gos-hex-zoom { transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .gos-hex-zoom:hover { transform: scale(1.12); } .cap { color: #555; font-size: 13px; margin: 2px 0 6px 0; } ")), # A plot rendered while the tab is in the background gets width 0 and shows # an error; nudge Shiny to re-measure when the tab becomes visible again. tags$script(HTML(" document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', function() { if (!document.hidden) { setTimeout(function() { window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')); }, 250); } }); ")), # Browsers bypass the service worker for navigations (HTML # spec: downloads have service-workers mode 'none'), so in Shinylive the # native download click reaches the static host and 404s. Fetch the file # through the service worker instead and hand it over as a blob. tags$script(HTML(" document.addEventListener('click', function(e) { var a = e.target && e.target.closest('a.shiny-download-link'); if (!a || !a.getAttribute('href')) return; e.preventDefault(); fetch(a.href).then(function(resp) { if (!resp.ok) throw new Error('HTTP ' + resp.status); var cd = resp.headers.get('content-disposition') || ''; var m = /filename\\*?=(?:UTF-8'')?\"?([^\";]+)\"?/i.exec(cd); var filename = m ? decodeURIComponent(m[1]) : (a.download || 'download'); return resp.blob().then(function(blob) { var url = URL.createObjectURL(blob); var tmp = document.createElement('a'); tmp.href = url; tmp.download = filename; document.body.appendChild(tmp); tmp.click(); tmp.remove(); setTimeout(function() { URL.revokeObjectURL(url); }, 4000); }); }).catch(function(err) { alert('Download failed: ' + err.message + '. Compute the results first, then try again.'); }); }, true); "))), div(style = "margin: 18px 0 6px 0; overflow: hidden;", a(href = "https://ausgis.github.io/geosimilarity/", target = "_blank", class = "gos-hex-zoom", title = "geosimilarity package documentation", style = "float: right; margin: 0 0 8px 18px; line-height: 0;", HTML(HEX_SVG)), h2("GOS calculator — geographically optimal similarity"), p(style = "margin-top: 10px;", "Geographically optimal similarity (GOS) predicts a variable at unknown ", "locations from the geographical configuration of covariates: it ", "measures how similar each prediction location is to every observation, ", "keeps only the most similar fraction ", HTML("κ"), " of observations — the optimal share ", HTML("λ"), " being the one that minimises cross-validation RMSE — and takes a ", "similarity-weighted average over them. The same similarities give a ", "prediction uncertainty at each location. Upload your samples (and, if ", "you have one, a prediction grid), assign the variable roles, and press ", "Compute.")), p(class = "citehead", "To cite the GOS (geographically optimal similarity) model in ", "publications, please use:"), div(class = "cite", "Song, Y. (2022). Geographically Optimal Similarity. ", em("Mathematical Geosciences, "), "55, 295–320. ", a(href = "https://doi.org/10.1007/s11004-022-10036-8", target = "_blank", "doi:10.1007/s11004-022-10036-8")), p(class = "note", "All computation runs locally in your browser (WebAssembly R) and is ", "computed by the CRAN package ", a(href = "https://cran.r-project.org/package=geosimilarity", target = "_blank", code("geosimilarity")), " (v3.9). Your data is never uploaded to any server."), sidebarLayout( sidebarPanel(width = 4, h4("1 · Data"), fileInput("file", "Sample CSV", accept = c(".csv", "text/csv")), fileInput("gridfile", "Prediction-grid CSV (optional)", accept = c(".csv", "text/csv")), actionButton("example", "Load example data (Zn, Western Australia)", class = "btn-sm"), div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 6px;", "Your data never leaves the browser — everything runs in ", "WebAssembly R. One row per location; up to ", format(MAX_SAMPLES, big.mark = ","), " samples and ", format(MAX_GRID, big.mark = ","), " grid cells. Without a prediction ", "grid the app predicts at held-out sample locations instead ", "(the maps are then skipped and only the accuracy tables shown)."), div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 6px;", "The example is the ", code("geosimilarity"), " built-in dataset: 894 ", "soil Zn samples and a 13,132-cell 1 km grid from the Leonora ", "mineral district, Western Australia (the paper's case study)."), hr(), h4("2 · Variable roles"), div(class = "varlab", "Response variable"), selectInput("var_y", NULL, choices = c("Select…" = "")), fluidRow( column(6, div(class = "varlab", "Longitude / x"), selectInput("var_lon", NULL, choices = c("Select…" = ""))), column(6, div(class = "varlab", "Latitude / y"), selectInput("var_lat", NULL, choices = c("Select…" = ""))) ), div(class = "varlab", "Covariates (at least 2)"), div(style = "max-height: 190px; overflow-y: auto; border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 4px; padding: 6px 10px; background: #fff;", checkboxGroupInput("var_x", NULL, choices = character(0))), div(class = "note", "Column names are free — nothing is guessed from them beyond the ", "initial pre-selection, which you can change. A prediction grid must ", "contain every covariate ticked here plus the two coordinate columns."), uiOutput("grid_check"), hr(), h4("3 · Preprocessing"), checkboxInput("dolog", "Log-transform the response", value = FALSE), checkboxInput("dooutlier", "Remove outliers (Tukey coef)", value = FALSE), conditionalPanel("input.dooutlier == true", numericInput("outcoef", NULL, value = 2.5, min = 1, max = 6, step = 0.1)), numericInput("thin", "Thin prediction grid: keep every n-th cell", value = 1, min = 1, max = 100, step = 1), div(class = "note", "Similarity is computed between every grid cell and every sample, so ", "the prediction time grows with both. Measured in a browser, the full ", "13,132-cell example grid takes about 2\u20133 minutes; thin it to 2 or 5 ", "while you are still choosing variables. On a regular grid the thinning strides ", "both axes, so the map stays a filled raster at a coarser resolution ", "(a little more than 1 cell in n is dropped). Thinning also changes ", "the numbers slightly, because the package derives the similarity ", "scale ", HTML("σ"), " from the observation and prediction ", "locations together."), hr(), h4(HTML("4 · Optimal similarity (κ) search")), textInput("kappas", "Candidate κ values (comma-separated)", value = KAPPA_TXT), fluidRow( column(6, numericInput("nrepeat", "Repeats", value = 3, min = 1, max = 20, step = 1)), column(6, numericInput("nsplit", "Training share", value = 0.5, min = 0.1, max = 0.9, step = 0.05)) ), div(class = "note", "Each κ is scored by repeated random split validation; λ is the κ ", "with the lowest mean RMSE. κ = 1 is the basic configuration ", "similarity (BCS) model, which uses every observation."), hr(), h4("5 · Uncertainty"), selectInput("zeta", HTML("Quantile ζ to map"), choices = ZETA_CHOICE, selected = "0.99"), div(class = "note", "Uncertainty is 1 − the ζ-quantile of the retained similarities, so ", "a smaller ζ gives a stricter (higher) uncertainty; ζ = 1 uses the ", "single most similar observation."), hr(), h4("6 · Compute"), actionButton("compute", "Compute GOS", class = "btn-primary"), div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 6px;", "The κ search dominates the runtime: it is one GOS fit per κ per ", "repeat, and the grid prediction that follows is a second pass over ", "every cell. Measured in a browser, the whole example run with these ", "defaults (six κ × 3 repeats over the full 13,132-cell grid) takes ", "roughly 4 minutes; each extra κ or repeat adds about 5 seconds.") ), mainPanel(width = 8, h4("Data preview — first 6 rows of the samples"), uiOutput("preview_ui"), verbatimTextOutput("summary", placeholder = TRUE), uiOutput("results_ui") ) ), tags$details(style = "margin: 16px 0;", tags$summary("Method notes & data format"), tags$ul( tags$li(HTML("GOS in one paragraph: for a prediction location, ", "each covariate contributes a Gaussian similarity to every ", "observation; the covariates are combined with a minimum operator, ", "so a location is only as similar as its least similar covariate. ", "Only the fraction κ of observations with the highest ", "similarity is kept, and the prediction is their similarity-weighted ", "mean. λ = argminκ RMSE(κ) from ", "repeated split validation; κ = 1 keeps everything and is the ", "BCS model. Uncertainty at a location is 1 minus the ζ-quantile ", "of the retained similarities.")), tags$li("All numbers come from the CRAN geosimilarity package running ", "in your browser (webR): gos(), gos_bestkappa() and ", "removeoutlier(), with cores = 1 (WebAssembly has no multiprocess)."), tags$li(HTML("Sample CSV: one row per observation; one numeric ", "response column; a longitude and a latitude column (used only for ", "the maps, not in the model); at least two numeric covariate ", "columns. Grid CSV: the same covariate and coordinate ", "columns, one row per prediction cell — no response column needed. ", "Rows with missing values in the selected columns are dropped and ", "reported.")), tags$li(HTML("Covariate selection is yours to make. The paper first ", "keeps covariates significantly correlated with the response and ", "then removes collinear ones (VIF < 4); this app does not do that ", "step for you.")), tags$li(HTML("The prediction is computed in a single pass over the ", "grid, not in chunks: the package derives the similarity scale ", "σ and the distance normaliser from all observation and ", "prediction locations together, so splitting the grid would change ", "the results. That is why the last step of the progress bar does not ", "advance.")), tags$li(HTML("The accuracy table uses the same random splits as the ", "κ search (seeds 1…repeats), so GOS, BCS and the linear model ", "are compared on identical training and test sets. Errors are ", "reported on the modelling scale, i.e. on the log response when the ", "log-transform box is ticked.")), tags$li(HTML("Kriging is deliberately out of scope here — it needs a ", "variogram model and a spatial-statistics stack that would triple ", "the download. See the ", "", "geosimilarity website and the reproduction tutorial for the ", "full five-model comparison.")) )) ) # -- Server ------------------------------------------------------------------- server <- function(input, output, session) { raw <- reactiveVal(NULL) # list(df, label) gridr <- reactiveVal(NULL) # list(df, label) numericish <- function(v) is.numeric(v) || (!all(is.na(v)) && !all(is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v))))) as_num <- function(v) if (is.numeric(v)) v else suppressWarnings(as.numeric(v)) # Load samples, then pre-select variable roles from the columns. populate <- function(df, label, roles = NULL) { names(df) <- trimws(names(df)) raw(list(df = df, label = label)) cols <- names(df) idish <- cols[cols == "" | grepl("^(id|gridid|fid|objectid)$", cols, ignore.case = TRUE)] usable <- setdiff(cols, idish) isnum <- vapply(df[usable], numericish, logical(1)) numc <- usable[isnum] guess <- function(pat) { h <- numc[grepl(pat, numc, ignore.case = TRUE)] if (length(h)) h[1] else "" } lon <- guess("^(lon|long|longitude|x|easting|xcoord)$") lat <- guess("^(lat|latitude|y|northing|ycoord)$") yv <- setdiff(numc, c(lon, lat)) yv <- if (length(yv)) yv[1] else "" xs <- setdiff(numc, c(lon, lat, yv)) if (!is.null(roles)) { lon <- roles$lon; lat <- roles$lat; yv <- roles$y; xs <- roles$x } updateSelectInput(session, "var_y", choices = c("Select…" = "", usable), selected = yv) updateSelectInput(session, "var_lon", choices = c("Select…" = "", usable), selected = lon) updateSelectInput(session, "var_lat", choices = c("Select…" = "", usable), selected = lat) updateCheckboxGroupInput(session, "var_x", choices = usable, selected = xs) } observeEvent(input$example, { grd <- utils::read.csv(EX_GRID, check.names = FALSE) gridr(list(df = grd, label = "geosimilarity grid (13,132 cells)")) populate(utils::read.csv(EX_SAMPLES, check.names = FALSE), "geosimilarity zn (894 soil samples, Leonora, WA)", roles = list(y = "Zn", lon = "Lon", lat = "Lat", x = EX_COVARS)) updateCheckboxInput(session, "dolog", value = TRUE) updateCheckboxInput(session, "dooutlier", value = TRUE) updateNumericInput(session, "outcoef", value = 2.5) updateNumericInput(session, "thin", value = 1) }) observeEvent(input$file, { df <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(input$file$datapath, check.names = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL) if (is.null(df)) { showNotification("Could not read that file as CSV.", type = "error") } else { populate(df, input$file$name) } }) observeEvent(input$gridfile, { df <- tryCatch(utils::read.csv(input$gridfile$datapath, check.names = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL) if (is.null(df)) { showNotification("Could not read the grid file as CSV.", type = "error") } else { names(df) <- trimws(names(df)) gridr(list(df = df, label = input$gridfile$name)) } }) # -- validated inputs ------------------------------------------------------- selection <- reactive({ r <- raw() validate(need(!is.null(r), "Load the example data or upload a sample CSV first.")) yv <- input$var_y lon <- input$var_lon lat <- input$var_lat xs <- setdiff(input$var_x, c(yv, lon, lat)) validate( need(nzchar(yv), "Select the response variable (2 · Variable roles)."), need(nzchar(lon) && nzchar(lat), "Select the longitude and latitude columns (2 · Variable roles)."), need(length(xs) >= MIN_COVARS, paste0("Tick at least ", MIN_COVARS, " covariates — GOS combines ", "them with a minimum operator, so a single covariate is ", "not a geographical configuration."))) list(y = yv, lon = lon, lat = lat, x = xs) }) # Working sample set: complete rows, optional log transform and outlier # removal (in that order, as in the package vignette). prepared <- reactive({ r <- raw(); s <- selection() used <- unique(c(s$y, s$lon, s$lat, s$x)) df <- r$df[, used, drop = FALSE] bad <- used[!vapply(df[used], numericish, logical(1))] validate(need(!length(bad), paste0( "These selected columns are not numeric: ", paste(bad, collapse = ", "), ". GOS needs numeric coordinates, response and covariates."))) for (cc in used) df[[cc]] <- as_num(df[[cc]]) keep <- stats::complete.cases(df) df <- df[keep, , drop = FALSE] dropped <- sum(!keep) logged <- isTRUE(input$dolog) if (logged) { validate(need(all(df[[s$y]] > 0), paste0( "The log-transform needs a strictly positive response; ", s$y, " has values <= 0."))) df[[s$y]] <- log(df[[s$y]]) } nout <- 0L if (isTRUE(input$dooutlier)) { cf <- input$outcoef validate(need(is.finite(cf) && cf > 0, "The outlier coefficient must be a positive number.")) k <- suppressMessages(geosimilarity::removeoutlier(df[[s$y]], coef = cf)) if (length(k)) { df <- df[-k, , drop = FALSE]; nout <- length(k) } } validate( need(nrow(df) >= MIN_SAMPLES, paste0("Only ", nrow(df), " usable samples — at least ", MIN_SAMPLES, " are needed.")), need(nrow(df) <= MAX_SAMPLES, paste0(format(nrow(df), big.mark = ","), " samples exceed the current limit of ", format(MAX_SAMPLES, big.mark = ","), " for the in-browser version. Subsample your data first."))) rownames(df) <- NULL list(dt = df, sel = s, logged = logged, dropped = dropped, nout = nout, label = r$label) }) # Prediction grid, validated against the chosen roles and thinned. gridprep <- reactive({ g <- gridr() if (is.null(g)) return(NULL) s <- selection() need_cols <- unique(c(s$lon, s$lat, s$x)) miss <- setdiff(need_cols, names(g$df)) validate(need(!length(miss), paste0( "The prediction grid is missing these columns: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), ". Either add them to the grid file or untick them above."))) df <- g$df for (cc in need_cols) df[[cc]] <- as_num(df[[cc]]) bad <- need_cols[!vapply(df[need_cols], is.numeric, logical(1))] validate(need(!length(bad), paste0( "These grid columns are not numeric: ", paste(bad, collapse = ", ")))) keep <- stats::complete.cases(df[, need_cols, drop = FALSE]) df <- df[keep, , drop = FALSE] dropped <- sum(!keep) nfull <- nrow(df) thin <- input$thin validate(need(is.finite(thin) && thin >= 1, "Grid thinning must be an integer of at least 1.")) thin <- as.integer(thin) df <- thin_grid(df, s$lon, s$lat, thin) validate( need(nrow(df) >= 1, "The prediction grid has no usable rows."), need(nrow(df) <= MAX_GRID, paste0(format(nrow(df), big.mark = ","), " grid cells exceed the current limit of ", format(MAX_GRID, big.mark = ","), " for the in-browser version. Raise the thinning factor to at least ", ceiling(nfull / MAX_GRID) + 1, "."))) rownames(df) <- NULL list(df = df, dropped = dropped, thin = thin, nfull = nfull, label = g$label) }) kappa_grid <- reactive({ v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric( strsplit(trimws(input$kappas), "[,;[:space:]]+")[[1]])) v <- v[!is.na(v)] validate( need(length(v) >= 2, "Give at least two candidate κ values, comma-separated."), need(all(v > 0 & v <= 1), "Every κ must be greater than 0 and at most 1.")) sort(unique(v)) }) cv_pars <- reactive({ nr <- input$nrepeat; ns <- input$nsplit validate( need(is.finite(nr) && nr >= 1 && nr <= 20, "Repeats must be between 1 and 20."), need(is.finite(ns) && ns >= 0.1 && ns <= 0.9, "The training share must be between 0.1 and 0.9.")) list(nrepeat = as.integer(nr), nsplit = ns) }) output$grid_check <- renderUI({ g <- gridr() if (is.null(g)) { return(div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 6px;", em("No prediction grid loaded — the app will predict at held-out ", "sample locations."))) } s <- tryCatch(selection(), error = function(e) NULL) if (is.null(s)) return(NULL) miss <- setdiff(unique(c(s$lon, s$lat, s$x)), names(g$df)) if (length(miss)) { div(class = "note warn", style = "margin-top: 6px;", "Grid file is missing: ", paste(miss, collapse = ", "), " — untick those covariates or supply a grid that has them.") } else { div(class = "note", style = "margin-top: 6px; color: #2c7;", "Grid file has all ", length(s$x), " covariates and both coordinates ", "(", format(nrow(g$df), big.mark = ","), " cells).") } }) # -- computation ------------------------------------------------------------ result <- eventReactive(input$compute, { p <- prepared() gp <- gridprep() ks_grid <- kappa_grid() cvp <- cv_pars() s <- p$sel res <- withProgress(message = "Computing GOS…", value = 0, { tryCatch({ setProgress(0.02, detail = "optimal similarity search") ks <- gos_kappa_search( p$dt, s$y, s$x, ks_grid, cvp$nrepeat, cvp$nsplit, progress = function(i, n, what) setProgress(0.02 + 0.50 * i / n, detail = what)) setProgress(0.52, detail = "accuracy comparison") acc <- gos_accuracy( p$dt, s$y, s$x, ks$lambda, cvp$nrepeat, cvp$nsplit, progress = function(i, n, what) setProgress(0.52 + 0.18 * i / n, detail = what)) f <- gos_formula(s$y, s$x) if (!is.null(gp)) { setProgress(0.72, detail = sprintf( "predicting %s grid cells in one pass — no progress possible, see the method notes", format(nrow(gp$df), big.mark = ","))) g <- geosimilarity::gos(f, data = p$dt, newdata = gp$df, kappa = ks$lambda, cores = 1) loc <- gp$df mode <- "grid" } else { setProgress(0.72, detail = "predicting held-out sample locations") idx <- cv_trainindex(nrow(p$dt), cvp$nsplit, 1) tr <- p$dt[idx, , drop = FALSE] loc <- p$dt[-idx, , drop = FALSE] g <- geosimilarity::gos(f, data = tr, newdata = loc, kappa = ks$lambda, cores = 1) mode <- "holdout" } setProgress(1, detail = "done") list(ks = ks, acc = acc, gos = g, loc = loc, mode = mode, prep = p, gp = gp, cvp = cvp) }, error = function(e) e) }) if (inherits(res, "error")) { showNotification(paste("Computation failed:", conditionMessage(res)), type = "error", duration = 14) return(NULL) } res }) # -- preview and summary ---------------------------------------------------- output$preview_ui <- renderUI({ if (is.null(raw())) return(div(class = "note", "Load the example data or upload a sample CSV to see its first rows ", "here.")) div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("preview")) }) output$preview <- renderTable({ r <- raw(); req(r) utils::head(r$df, 6) }, striped = TRUE, digits = 4, class = "data") output$summary <- renderText({ r <- raw() if (is.null(r)) return("No data loaded yet.") s <- tryCatch(selection(), error = function(e) NULL) if (is.null(s)) return(sprintf("Samples: %s (%d rows, %d columns)\nAssign the variable roles in [2 · Variable roles].", r$label, nrow(r$df), ncol(r$df))) p <- tryCatch(prepared(), error = function(e) NULL) g <- tryCatch(gridr(), error = function(e) NULL) head <- sprintf( "Samples: %s\nResponse: %s%s Coordinates: %s, %s\nCovariates (%d): %s\nPrediction grid: %s", r$label, s$y, if (isTRUE(input$dolog)) " (log-transformed)" else "", s$lon, s$lat, length(s$x), paste(s$x, collapse = ", "), if (is.null(g)) "none — held-out samples will be used" else sprintf("%s (%s cells)", g$label, format(nrow(g$df), big.mark = ","))) if (is.null(p)) return(head) head <- sprintf("%s\nUsable samples: %d (%d incomplete rows dropped, %d outliers removed)", head, nrow(p$dt), p$dropped, p$nout) res <- if (input$compute > 0) tryCatch(result(), error = function(e) NULL) else NULL if (is.null(res)) return(paste0(head, "\nSet the parameters and press [Compute GOS].")) sprintf("%s\nComputed: lambda = %s over %d candidate kappa values, %d repeats at a %.0f%% training share; %s. geosimilarity %s.", head, format(res$ks$lambda, trim = TRUE), nrow(res$ks$cvmean), res$cvp$nrepeat, 100 * res$cvp$nsplit, if (res$mode == "grid") sprintf("%s grid cells predicted%s", format(nrow(res$loc), big.mark = ","), if (res$gp$thin > 1) sprintf(" (thinned from %s, factor %d)", format(res$gp$nfull, big.mark = ","), res$gp$thin) else "") else sprintf("%s held-out sample locations predicted", format(nrow(res$loc), big.mark = ",")), as.character(utils::packageVersion("geosimilarity"))) }) # -- results layout Right: prediction uncertainty at ζ = %s (1 − the ζ-quantile of the retained similarities); its colour ramp is clipped at the 99th percentile, the top class is marked ≥.", format(r$ks$lambda, trim = TRUE), if (r$prep$logged) ", back-transformed with exp() to the original units" else "", input$zeta)), plotOutput("fig_maps", height = "350px"), dlrow(downloadButton("dl_fig2_png", "Figure 2 PNG"), downloadButton("dl_fig2_pdf", "Figure 2 PDF (vector)")) ) else div(class = "note", style = "margin: 14px 0;", em("No prediction grid was supplied, so the maps are skipped. The ", "prediction below is made at the held-out sample locations of the ", "first split instead; upload a grid CSV in [1 · Data] to get the ", "maps.")), h4("Table 1 — accuracy on held-out data"), div(class = "cap", sprintf("Mean over %d repeats of the same %.0f/%.0f splits used for the κ search, so all three models see identical training and test sets. Errors are on the %s scale.", r$cvp$nrepeat, 100 * r$cvp$nsplit, 100 * (1 - r$cvp$nsplit), if (r$prep$logged) "log-response" else "response")), div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("tab_acc")), dlrow(downloadButton("dl_tab1_csv", "Accuracy table CSV")), h4(HTML("Table 2 — the κ–RMSE numbers behind Figure 1")), div(class = "scrollx", tableOutput("tab_kappa")), dlrow(downloadButton("dl_tab2_csv", "κ–RMSE table CSV")), h4("Full prediction"), div(class = "cap", if (r$mode == "grid") sprintf("%s grid cells with the GOS prediction%s and all six uncertainty columns (ζ = 0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.995, 0.999, 1) joined to the grid you supplied.", format(nrow(r$loc), big.mark = ","), if (r$prep$logged) " on both the modelling and original scale" else "") else sprintf("%s held-out sample locations with the GOS prediction%s and all six uncertainty columns.", format(nrow(r$loc), big.mark = ","), if (r$prep$logged) " on both the modelling and original scale" else "")), dlrow(downloadButton("dl_pred_csv", "Prediction + uncertainty CSV")) ) }) # -- figures ---------------------------------------------------------------- zeta_num <- reactive(as.numeric(input$zeta)) unc_vec <- function(r) r$gos[[ZETA_COL[[as.character(zeta_num())]]]] pred_vec <- function(r) if (r$prep$logged) exp(r$gos$pred) else r$gos$pred draw_fig1 <- function(r) plot_kappa_rmse(r$ks$cvmean, r$ks$lambda) draw_fig2 <- function(r) plot_gos_maps( r$loc[[r$prep$sel$lon]], r$loc[[r$prep$sel$lat]], pred_vec(r), unc_vec(r), zeta_num(), pred_title = "GOS") output$fig_kappa <- renderPlot({ r <- result(); req(r); draw_fig1(r) }) output$fig_maps <- renderPlot({ r <- result(); req(r); draw_fig2(r) }) # -- tables ----------------------------------------------------------------- fmt <- function(x, d = 4) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f"), x)) output$tab_acc <- renderTable({ r <- result(); req(r) a <- r$acc data.frame(Model = a$Model, MAE = fmt(a$MAE), RMSE = fmt(a$RMSE), `Error reduction by GOS — MAE (%)` = fmt(a[["Error reduction by GOS - MAE (%)"]], 2), `Error reduction by GOS — RMSE (%)` = fmt(a[["Error reduction by GOS - RMSE (%)"]], 2), check.names = FALSE) }, striped = TRUE, class = "data", align = "lrrrr") output$tab_kappa <- renderTable({ r <- result(); req(r) cv <- r$ks$cvmean data.frame(`κ` = num_lab(cv$kappa), `Cross-validation RMSE` = fmt(cv$rmse, 6), `Note` = ifelse(cv$kappa == r$ks$lambda, "λ (optimal)", ifelse(cv$kappa == 1, "BCS (all observations)", "")), check.names = FALSE) }, striped = TRUE, class = "data", align = "rrl") # -- downloads -------------------------------------------------------------- dl_png <- function(name, draw_fn, w, h) downloadHandler( filename = function() name, content = function(f) { r <- result(); req(r) grDevices::png(f, width = w, height = h, res = 220) on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()) draw_fn(r) }) dl_pdf <- function(name, draw_fn, w_in, h_in) downloadHandler( filename = function() name, content = function(f) { r <- result(); req(r) grDevices::pdf(f, width = w_in, height = h_in, useDingbats = FALSE) on.exit(grDevices::dev.off()) draw_fn(r) }) dl_csv <- function(name, table_fn) downloadHandler( filename = function() name, content = function(f) { r <- result(); req(r) utils::write.csv(table_fn(r), f, row.names = FALSE, na = "") }) output$dl_fig1_png <- dl_png("gos-kappa-rmse.png", draw_fig1, 1500, 1300) output$dl_fig1_pdf <- dl_pdf("gos-kappa-rmse.pdf", draw_fig1, 6.6, 5.7) output$dl_fig2_png <- dl_png("gos-prediction-uncertainty.png", draw_fig2, 2400, 1080) output$dl_fig2_pdf <- dl_pdf("gos-prediction-uncertainty.pdf", draw_fig2, 11, 4.95) output$dl_tab1_csv <- dl_csv("gos-accuracy.csv", function(r) r$acc) output$dl_tab2_csv <- dl_csv("gos-kappa-rmse.csv", function(r) { cv <- r$ks$cvmean data.frame(kappa = cv$kappa, cv_rmse = cv$rmse, optimal = cv$kappa == r$ks$lambda) }) output$dl_pred_csv <- dl_csv("gos-prediction.csv", function(r) { out <- r$loc # in held-out mode `loc` carries the preprocessed samples, so the response # column is already log-transformed — say so in its name if (r$mode == "holdout" && r$prep$logged) { yv <- r$prep$sel$y names(out)[names(out) == yv] <- paste0(yv, "_log_observed") } out$gos_pred <- r$gos$pred if (r$prep$logged) out$gos_pred_original_scale <- exp(r$gos$pred) for (cc in ZETA_COL) out[[cc]] <- r$gos[[cc]] out }) } shinyApp(ui, server)

name: gos-plots.R
content:
# =============================================================================
# gos-plots.R — numeric driver + paper-style figures for the GOS calculator
# =============================================================================
# Two layers, both shared by app.R and tools/test-figures.R:
#
#   * compute  — thin wrappers around the CRAN geosimilarity package
#                (gos / gos_bestkappa / removeoutlier). No re-implementation of
#                the method: every number below comes out of the package.
#   * figures  — base graphics only, in the house style: box() on every panel,
#                pty = "s" for maps and the kappa curve, Greek letters through
#                plotmath so the vector PDF export is cross-platform.
#
# Method: Song, Y. (2022). Geographically Optimal Similarity.
# Mathematical Geosciences 55, 295-320. doi:10.1007/s11004-022-10036-8
# =============================================================================

ACCENT      <- "#b03a2e"   # GOS brick red (design.md section 5)
ACCENT_SOFT <- "#fbeeec"

# zeta -> the package's uncertainty column for that quantile
ZETA_COL <- c("0.9" = "uncertainty90", "0.95" = "uncertainty95",
              "0.99" = "uncertainty99", "0.995" = "uncertainty99.5",
              "0.999" = "uncertainty99.9", "1" = "uncertainty100")

# -- compute ------------------------------------------------------------------

# Backtick every name so non-syntactic column names work (verified in OPGD).
gos_formula <- function(y, xs) stats::as.formula(
  paste0("`", y, "` ~ ", paste0("`", xs, "`", collapse = " + ")))

# gos_bestkappa()'s own split for repeat `seed`, replicated verbatim so the
# accuracy table below is computed on exactly the same splits as the kappa
# search (gos_bestkappa uses seeds 1..nrepeat and floor(nsplit * n)).
cv_trainindex <- function(n, nsplit, seed) {
  set.seed(seed)
  sample.int(n = n, size = floor(nsplit * n), replace = FALSE)
}

# Optimal similarity search. One gos_bestkappa() call per kappa instead of a
# single multi-kappa call, purely so a progress bar can move: the seeds are
# per-repeat, not per-kappa, so the two give bit-identical cvmean tables
# (verified offline, see design.md "构建与验证记录").
gos_kappa_search <- function(dt, y, xs, kappas, nrepeat, nsplit,
                             progress = NULL) {
  f <- gos_formula(y, xs)
  rows <- lapply(seq_along(kappas), function(i) {
    if (!is.null(progress))
      progress(i, length(kappas),
               sprintf("kappa = %s", format(kappas[i], trim = TRUE)))
    as.data.frame(geosimilarity::gos_bestkappa(
      f, data = dt, kappa = kappas[i], nrepeat = nrepeat,
      nsplit = nsplit, cores = 1)$cvmean)
  })
  cv <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  cv <- cv[order(cv$kappa), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(cv) <- NULL
  list(cvmean = cv, lambda = cv$kappa[which.min(cv$rmse)[1]])
}

# Held-out accuracy of GOS (kappa = lambda), BCS (kappa = 1) and a
# multivariate linear regression, averaged over `nrepeat` repeats of the same
# train/test splits.
gos_accuracy <- function(dt, y, xs, lambda, nrepeat, nsplit, progress = NULL) {
  f <- gos_formula(y, xs)
  n <- nrow(dt)
  spec  <- list(GOS = lambda, BCS = 1, MLR = "lm")
  total <- length(spec) * nrepeat
  done  <- 0L
  one <- function(mname) {
    kappa <- spec[[mname]]
    per <- vapply(seq_len(nrepeat), function(r) {
      idx <- cv_trainindex(n, nsplit, r)
      tr  <- dt[idx, , drop = FALSE]
      te  <- dt[-idx, , drop = FALSE]
      p <- if (identical(kappa, "lm"))
        as.numeric(stats::predict(stats::lm(f, data = tr), newdata = te))
      else
        geosimilarity::gos(f, data = tr, newdata = te,
                           kappa = kappa, cores = 1)$pred
      done <<- done + 1L
      if (!is.null(progress))
        progress(done, total, sprintf("%s, repeat %d/%d", mname, r, nrepeat))
      e <- te[[y]] - p
      c(mae = mean(abs(e)), rmse = sqrt(mean(e^2)))
    }, numeric(2))
    rowMeans(per)
  }
  m <- vapply(names(spec), one, numeric(2))          # 2 x 3
  g <- m[, "GOS"]
  data.frame(
    Model = c(sprintf("GOS (kappa = %s)", format(lambda, trim = TRUE)),
              "BCS (kappa = 1)", "Multivariate linear regression"),
    MAE  = m["mae", ],
    RMSE = m["rmse", ],
    `Error reduction by GOS - MAE (%)`  =
      c(NA, (m["mae", -1]  - g["mae"])  / m["mae", -1]  * 100),
    `Error reduction by GOS - RMSE (%)` =
      c(NA, (m["rmse", -1] - g["rmse"]) / m["rmse", -1] * 100),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
}

# Keep roughly one prediction cell in `n`. Taking literally every n-th row of a
# raster leaves a moire of stripes, so on a lattice the two axes are strided
# instead (sx * sy >= n): the retained cells stay contiguous, tile_geom() picks
# up the coarser spacing, and the map is a proper lower-resolution raster.
# Scattered (non-lattice) prediction points fall back to every n-th row.
thin_grid <- function(df, xcol, ycol, n) {
  n <- as.integer(n)
  if (is.na(n) || n <= 1L || !nrow(df)) return(df)
  ux <- sort(unique(df[[xcol]]))
  uy <- sort(unique(df[[ycol]]))
  if (length(ux) > 2 && length(uy) > 2 &&
      length(ux) * length(uy) <= 25 * nrow(df)) {
    sx <- as.integer(ceiling(sqrt(n)))
    sy <- max(1L, as.integer(ceiling(n / sx)))
    out <- df[df[[xcol]] %in% ux[seq(1L, length(ux), by = sx)] &
              df[[ycol]] %in% uy[seq(1L, length(uy), by = sy)], , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(out)) return(out)
  }
  df[seq(1L, nrow(df), by = n), , drop = FALSE]
}

# -- figures: shared helpers --------------------------------------------------

# Sequential ramp with the extremes trimmed, so the low end is not paper white
# and the high end not pure black. Base R has no "Magma"; Rocket is the
# magma-like half of the Rocket/Mako pair used by the package vignette.
gos_pal <- function(n, name) {
  grDevices::hcl.colors(n + 24, name, rev = TRUE)[seq_len(n) + 6L]
}

# Value -> colour index, clamped to the (possibly clipped) display range.
pal_index <- function(v, zlim, n) {
  i <- floor((v - zlim[1]) / diff(zlim) * n) + 1L
  pmin(pmax(i, 1L), n)
}

num_lab <- function(v) format(v, trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE)

# Is this a filled lattice (draw tiles) or scattered points (draw squares)?
tile_geom <- function(x, y) {
  ux <- sort(unique(signif(x, 12)))
  uy <- sort(unique(signif(y, 12)))
  span <- function(v) { r <- diff(range(v)); if (r > 0) r else 1 }
  dx <- if (length(ux) > 1) stats::median(diff(ux)) else span(x) / 20
  dy <- if (length(uy) > 1) stats::median(diff(uy)) else span(y) / 20
  if (!is.finite(dx) || dx <= 0) dx <- span(x) / 20
  if (!is.finite(dy) || dy <= 0) dy <- span(y) / 20
  list(dx = dx, dy = dy,
       lattice = length(ux) * length(uy) <= 25 * length(x))
}

# One square map panel. The fixed aspect ratio letterboxes the map inside its
# cell, so the title is drawn in data coordinates just above the mapped extent
# (a margin title would float far above it).
draw_gos_map <- function(x, y, v, pal, zlim, title_expr, cex_title = 1.35) {
  gm  <- tile_geom(x, y)
  col <- pal[pal_index(v, zlim, length(pal))]
  xr  <- range(x) + c(-1, 1) * gm$dx / 2
  yr  <- range(y) + c(-1, 1) * gm$dy / 2
  graphics::par(mar = c(0.4, 0.4, 2.4, 0.4), pty = "s")
  graphics::plot(NULL, xlim = xr, ylim = yr, xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
                 asp = 1 / cospi(mean(y) / 180), axes = FALSE,
                 xlab = "", ylab = "")
  if (gm$lattice) {
    # 1% overlap: abutting borderless rects leave hairline seams in vector
    # PDF output, and the overlap is far below one screen pixel
    hx <- gm$dx * 0.505
    hy <- gm$dy * 0.505
    graphics::rect(x - hx, y - hy, x + hx, y + hy, col = col, border = NA)
  } else {
    graphics::points(x, y, col = col, pch = 15,
                     cex = max(0.25, min(1.1, 90 / sqrt(length(x)))))
  }
  graphics::box(col = "grey35")
  graphics::text(mean(xr), yr[2] + 0.035 * diff(yr), title_expr,
                 adj = c(0.5, 0), cex = cex_title, xpd = NA)
  # device coordinates of the panel, so the colour bar can line up with it
  invisible(graphics::grconvertY(yr, "user", "ndc"))
}

# Vertical colour bar in its own layout cell, ticks and labels on the right.
# `clipped` appends ">=" to the top label when the ramp saturates. `align` is
# the NDC y-range returned by draw_gos_map: the square map panel letterboxes
# inside its cell, so the bar is matched to the map box rather than the cell.
draw_colorbar <- function(zlim, pal, clipped = FALSE, align = NULL) {
  n <- length(pal)
  graphics::par(mar = c(0.4, 0.2, 2.4, 0.2), pty = "m")
  graphics::plot(NULL, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1), xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i",
                 axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  frac <- c(0.10, 0.86)
  if (!is.null(align)) {
    f <- graphics::grconvertY(align, "ndc", "user")
    if (all(is.finite(f)) && diff(f) > 0.05) frac <- f
  }
  yb <- seq(frac[1], frac[2], length.out = n + 1L)
  ov <- diff(yb)[1] * 0.25                # overlap: no hairlines in the PDF
  graphics::rect(0.04, pmax(yb[-(n + 1L)] - ov, frac[1]), 0.40,
                 pmin(yb[-1L] + ov, frac[2]), col = pal, border = NA,
                 xpd = NA)
  graphics::rect(0.04, frac[1], 0.40, frac[2], border = "grey35", lwd = 0.8,
                 xpd = NA)
  at <- pretty(zlim, 5)
  at <- at[at >= zlim[1] & at <= zlim[2]]
  yp <- frac[1] + (at - zlim[1]) / diff(zlim) * diff(frac)
  graphics::segments(0.40, yp, 0.48, yp, col = "grey35")
  lab <- num_lab(at)
  # The base pdf() device has no U+2265 in its default font, so the ">=" of a
  # clipped ramp is drawn with plotmath (symbol font) instead of a literal.
  top <- if (clipped && length(lab)) which.max(at) else 0L
  ord <- setdiff(seq_along(lab), top)
  graphics::text(0.53, yp[ord], lab[ord], adj = c(0, 0.5), cex = 1.0, xpd = NA)
  if (top)
    graphics::text(0.53, yp[top], bquote("" >= .(lab[top])), adj = c(0, 0.5),
                   cex = 1.0, xpd = NA)
}

# -- Figure 1: kappa vs cross-validation RMSE (paper Fig. 7) -------------------

# The default kappa grid is geometric (0.01 ... 1), so a linear axis crushes
# two thirds of the points against the origin; switch to log10 when the grid
# spans more than a factor of 20. Ticks sit on the kappa values themselves,
# greedily thinned so labels never collide.
plot_kappa_rmse <- function(cvmean, lambda) {
  k <- cvmean$kappa
  r <- cvmean$rmse
  uselog <- length(k) >= 4 && min(k) > 0 && max(k) / min(k) >= 20
  tx <- if (uselog) log10(k) else k
  xr <- range(tx) + c(-1, 1) * max(diff(range(tx)), 1e-9) * 0.06
  yr <- range(r) + c(-1, 1) * max(diff(range(r)), 1e-9) * 0.12
  op <- graphics::par(mar = c(4.4, 5.0, 1.4, 1.4), mgp = c(3.0, 0.8, 0),
                      pty = "s", cex.lab = 1.15)
  on.exit(graphics::par(op))
  graphics::plot(NULL, xlim = xr, ylim = yr, axes = FALSE,
                 xlab = if (uselog) expression(kappa~~"(log scale)")
                        else expression(kappa),
                 ylab = "Cross-validation RMSE")
  graphics::lines(tx, r, lwd = 1.6)
  graphics::points(tx, r, pch = 16, cex = 1.15)
  i <- which(k == lambda)[1]
  graphics::points(tx[i], r[i], pch = 16, cex = 2.0, col = ACCENT)
  graphics::points(tx[i], r[i], pch = 1, cex = 2.0, col = "black", lwd = 1.2)
  lam <- bquote(lambda == .(format(lambda, trim = TRUE)))
  hw  <- graphics::strwidth(lam, cex = 1.25) / 2
  graphics::text(min(max(tx[i], xr[1] + hw), xr[2] - hw),
                 r[i] - 0.055 * diff(yr), lam,
                 adj = c(0.5, 1), cex = 1.25, col = ACCENT)
  # x ticks on the kappa values; labels thinned outwards from lambda so the
  # optimum is always labelled and no two labels collide (base axis() would
  # silently drop overlapping labels, and could drop lambda's).
  labs <- num_lab(k)
  wid  <- graphics::strwidth(labs)
  keep <- i
  for (j in c(rev(seq_len(i - 1L)), seq_len(length(k))[-seq_len(i)])) {
    if (all(abs(tx[j] - tx[keep]) > (wid[j] + wid[keep]) / 2 * 1.25))
      keep <- c(keep, j)
  }
  keep <- sort(keep)
  graphics::axis(1, at = tx, labels = FALSE, tcl = -0.25)
  graphics::axis(1, at = tx[keep], labels = labs[keep], tcl = -0.45,
                 cex.axis = 1.0)
  graphics::axis(2, las = 1, cex.axis = 1.0)
  graphics::box()
}

# -- Figure 2: GOS prediction map and uncertainty map -------------------------

# `pred` is already on the reporting scale (back-transformed by the caller when
# the response was log-transformed). Uncertainty is heavily right-skewed, so
# its ramp is clipped at the 99th percentile and the top label marked ">=".
plot_gos_maps <- function(x, y, pred, unc, zeta, pred_title = "GOS",
                          n_col = 200L) {
  pal_p <- gos_pal(n_col, "Rocket")
  pal_u <- gos_pal(n_col, "Mako")
  zp <- range(pred, finite = TRUE)
  if (diff(zp) <= 0) zp <- zp + c(-0.5, 0.5)
  umax <- stats::quantile(unc, 0.99, names = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE)
  zu <- c(min(unc, na.rm = TRUE), umax)
  clipped <- umax < max(unc, na.rm = TRUE) * (1 - 1e-12)
  if (diff(zu) <= 0) { zu <- range(unc, finite = TRUE); clipped <- FALSE }
  if (diff(zu) <= 0) zu <- zu + c(0, 1e-6)

  op <- graphics::par(c("mar", "pty", "mfrow"))
  on.exit({ graphics::layout(1); graphics::par(op) })
  graphics::layout(matrix(1:4, nrow = 1), widths = c(1, 0.34, 1, 0.34))
  a <- draw_gos_map(x, y, pred, pal_p, zp, pred_title)
  draw_colorbar(zp, pal_p, align = a)
  a <- draw_gos_map(x, y, unc, pal_u, zu,
                    bquote(GOS ~ (zeta == .(format(zeta, trim = TRUE)))))
  draw_colorbar(zu, pal_u, clipped = clipped, align = a)
}
